headline: Seven-Month-Old AI Startup Eyes $2B Valuation, Time Zone Permitting
subheadline: Upscale AI has found the optimal strategy: launch, raise, repeat, before anyone remembers what you actually do.
source_headline: Upscale AI in talks to raise at $2B valuation, says report
body_html:
Upscale AI, which launched approximately seven months ago—a timeframe shorter than most software beta cycles—is reportedly in talks to raise its third funding round at a $2 billion valuation. For context, this means the company will have been valued at $2 billion per month of existence. The math is intentional.

The AI infrastructure category has become a financial ouroboros where every new entrant immediately becomes a potential "unicorn" because the category itself hasn't stopped being hot. Investors, terrified of missing the next OpenAI, now treat "infrastructure for AI" the way they treated "cloud for X" in 2015—as an automatic wealth creator. Upscale's third round in seven months suggests a company either growing so explosibly that venture velocity is a feature, or one that VCs believe will exist long enough to exit before reality checks.

The press release probably mentions "category-defining" and "unprecedented demand." The Series A probably happened four months ago. The Series B was last month. The Series C is happening now because momentum is self-referential when everyone is running on fumes and hope.

By the time you finish reading this, Upscale will likely have announced a $5 billion Series D at a non-dilutive valuation increase, and nobody will ask why.
glossary_definition: The practice of raising consecutive funding rounds in accelerating intervals to outpace any meaningful assessment of whether the company is worth anything.
